episode.title: The Mechanics of a Quiet, Fast Bike

feed.description: Mountain biking talk: trails, technique, gear, and the people who build the ride.
feed.title: Singletrack Sessions

bullets: Chain wear is the single best leading indicator of how soon you'll be replacing cassettes — a pattern that holds across multiple teams.
Most mystery creaks are solved by cleaning contact surfaces and retorquing to spec, not by replacing parts.
A bike should feel quiet and predictable so your attention stays on the trail — once internalized, the rest of the decisions get easier.
Suspension service intervals are a risk management decision; ignoring them leads to rebuilding from scratch a year later.
The framing matters because it tells you which tradeoffs you're making — the second-order effect is the part most people miss.
Adopting a platform like Spok and Wrench makes the tradeoff visible in the flow of maintenance decisions.
The one heuristic to try this week: pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks; the rest is iteration.
